ruleName: Ball hits the flagstick or the person tending it
title: Flagstick Used To Stop The Ball – What's The Penalty?
question: If the flagstick is deliberately placed behind the hole to stop your ball, and your ball hits it, what is the ruling?

choices.text: No penalty, play as it lies
Two penalty strokes and you must replay the stroke
Move the flagstick and keep playing
Add one penalty stroke and continue

explanation: If someone sets the flagstick behind the hole on purpose to stop the ball and your ball hits it, you get a two stroke penalty and must replay the shot, as the previous stroke does not count.

juniorVersion.title: Putting the Flagstick Behind the Hole On Purpose
juniorVersion.question: If someone puts the flagstick behind the hole to stop your ball and your ball hits it, what happens?

choices.text: No penalty, play from where your ball stopped
You get 2 penalty shots and you must hit again from the same place
Just move the flagstick and keep going
Add one penalty shot and keep playing

juniorVersion.explanation: If someone puts the flagstick behind the hole to try to stop your ball, and your ball hits it, you must add 2 penalty shots and play your shot again. Your first shot does not count.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The stick with a flag that shows where the hole is on the green.
Extra shots added to your score if you break a rule.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind children that putting or holding the flagstick anywhere to stop a moving ball is not allowed. The flag can be in or taken out, but it can't be used to block the ball on purpose.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids may think it's okay to use the flagstick to help stop the ball.
They may not know you must replay the shot, not just take a penalty.
